newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen higher if PPI holds no surprises.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen higher if PPI holds no surprises.

text.p: Wall Street stocks should open mixed to slightly higher on Wednesday, provided a closely watched barometer of inflation holds no nasty surprises.

The U.S. Producer Price Index (PPI) is due to be reported by the Labor Department at 0830 EST/1330 GMT. U.S. economists in a Reuters survey expect a 0.2-percent rise compared with a 0.2-percent advance in September.
"Unless there's a major surprise in the PPI, which I don't suspect, we'll be off to the races today," said Peter Cardillo, Westfalia Investments director of research.
The PPI core rate, which excludes volatile food and energy items, is seen up 0.1 percent.
"It's a very strong market and although somewhere we should see a down day, I think we can can continue to make records for the rest of the week," he said.
The Dow rose 10 on Tuesday to about 6266, its fifth straight record, the longest string of Dow records since the seven-session streak from February 5-13.
The long bond was up 3/32 to yield 6.44 percent ahead of the opening of trading for stocks. Standard & Poor's December futures were slightly higher, up 0.5 to 732.5.

"There are so many good things happening right now, low interest rates and the Washington honeymoon strengthening between the President and Congress. With rates under 6.5 percent, it's difficult to make a case the market will give up in any big way soon," he said.
Cardillo said today's meeting of the Federal Reserve's panel which makes decisions on interest rates was considered a "non-event" by Wall Street, since no change in fiscal policy is expected.
On Thursday, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) will be reported at 0830 EST/1330 GMT by the Labor Department. It is expected to rise about 0.3 percent with the core rate rising by the same amount.
Tokyo stocks were beseiged by profit-taking as well as selling of futures contracts, with the Nikkei 225 falling 227 to 20,979.
In London, the FTSE-100 stock index fell 5.9 to 3928.4. U.S. shares in London were steady to slightly firmer although trading was light ahead of the release of the PPI.
The dollar was firm against the mark and doing better against the yen in European trading.

USAir Group Inc may be getting a new name and a new paint job, but the company has a much larger problem to face: it has the highest cost of doing business in the industry, according to the New York Times Marketplace column.
Some wonder if HFS Inc's buying spree is postive in the Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column.
Before the beginning of trading, Westinghouse Inc said it would split into two units, a broadcasting company and a separate industrial company and cut 1,100 jobs.
